Final for Publication

Application Number: 23048-T1

SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE | ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
2553-65 W. MADISON ST. CHICAGO,

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated along the Madison Street Bus
Corridor and within 1,900’ from the Green Line station at S. California Ave. and within 2,000‘
from the Blue Line station at S. Western Ave. The property is currently an unimproved, vacant
parcel. The Applicant intends to redevelop this property with a new 4-story mixed-use building
with commercial space on the ground floor and 42 dwelling units above, with 20 interior parking
spaces. The Applicant needs a zoning change to a B3-3 Community Shopping District with
optional variation for rear setback reduction and administrative adjustment relief for TSL parking
reduction, to comply with the standards and the bulk requirements of the Ordinance.

Project Zoning Change from Ct-2 Neighborhood Commercial District to
Description: B3-3 Community Shopping District

Use: Mixed-Use Building with 42 Dwelling Units and 20 parking spaces.
Lot Area: 138’ x 123’ = 16,974 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 3.0

Floor Area: 45,650 SF (see plans attached)

Density: 404 Square Feet per DU

Off- Street Parking: Parking spaces: 20 (see administrative adjustment request below)

Setbacks: Front: 0°
Side: 0° (each side)
Rear: 0’ (see variation request below)

Building Height: | 56°-5’ (to the top of the roof top enclosures per the attached plans)

L If required the Applicant will comply with the following Section: 17-3-0307 Exceptions:
1. Any application seeking a zoning map amendment, pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, in

order to establish a residential, day care, hospital, parks and recreation, school, eating and
drinking establishment with an outdoor patio or outdoor assembly use that is proposed to
be established within 660' of any (a) windrow composting facility, (b) intensive
manufacturing, production and industrial service use, (c) Class III, Class IVA, Class [VB
and Class V recycling facility, (d) warehousing, wholesaling, and freight movement use,
(e) container storage, (f) freight terminal, (g) outdoor storage of raw material as a
principal use, (h) waste-related use, or (i) manganese-bearing material operation use may
be allowed only if farther reviewed and approved in accordance with the special use
procedures of Section 17-13-0900, unless it otherwise meets a planned development
threshold of Section 17-8-0500.

IL. The Applicant will comply with Section 17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served
Locations, should such provisions be determined as applicable:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B.
The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated along the Madison Street
Bus Corridor and within 1,900’ from the Green Line station at S. California Ave. and within
2,000° from the Blue Line station at S. Western Ave.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504. except

paragraph H if the project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if
the land use is designated in a non-commercial use group. pertaining to pedestrian streets and

pedestrian retail streets. even if the project is not located along a pedestrian street or a
pedestrian retail street:
The subject property is not located along Pedestrian Street or Pedestrian Retail Street;
however, the project complies with the following criteria:
a. The entire building fagade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.
b. The project complies with the requirements of Section 17-3-0504-C Transparency
standards (minimum of 60% of the street- facing building facade between 4 feet and 10
feet in height will be comprised of clear, non-reflective windows that allow views of
indoor commercial space or product display areas; the bottom of any window or product
display window used to satisfy this requirement will not be more than 4.5 feet above the
adjacent sidewalk; and product display windows used to satisfy these requirements will
have a minimum height of 4 feet and be internally lighted)
c. The building will have a primary entrance door facing Madison Street.
d. All off-street parking spaces will be located inside the principal building and will not be
visible from the right-of-way.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development
Guide: Station Area Typology. and any other station-specific plans. designs or guidelines

adopted by the Chicago Plan Commission:
This Criteria is not applicable to this project

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of
the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-

0207 with any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole number. unless
additional parking spaces are approved as an administrative adjustment under the provisions
of Section 17-13-1003-EE: and


Final for Publication

With this proposed redevelopment, the Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is less
than 50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in
Section 17-10-0208. Consequently, the Applicant is requesting an Administrative Adjustment
via Optional Relief (see below) to decrease the parking from 21 spaces required to 20 parking
spaces proposed, which is in line with the TSL parking reduction policies.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the
Chicago Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of Transportation is
authorized to issue Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules consistent with this

section.
This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

III. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D — a Type
1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council
approval of a Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent
review otherwise required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided
that no Type 1 application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

1. With this Type 1 Rezoning, the Applicant also seeks relief for Administrative Adjustment
under section 17-13-1003-EE, from the parking requirements of Section 17-10-0102-B
and 17-10-0207-C, to decrease the on-site parking requirements from 21 parking spaces
required to 20 parking spaces, as proposed.

2. The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from rear
setback requirements of Section 17-3-0405 Rear Setbacks, which states that for floors
containing dwelling units, the minimum rear setback is 30 feet. To mitigate site planning
hardships on this substandard depth lot, the Applicant requests a reduction in the required
rear setback from 30 feet required to 0 feet proposed.

IV. The Applicant is seeking all the necessary relief, as allowed by the Zoning
Ordinance, for the proposed redevelopment of this vacant lot, per the attached Type
1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

(1) Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would
impose undue practical difficulties and unnecessary hardship on the subject property. The
parcel has remained vacant and underutilized for an extended period and is presently owned
by the City of Chicago. The Applicant is in the process of acquiring the property from the
City, thereby returning it to the tax rolls and restoring it to productive economic use.
Furthermore, the subject property is characterized by a substandard lot depth of only 123
feet, which materially limits the ability to accommodate a conforming building footprint,
required setbacks, parking, and site circulation in a manner consistent with the Ordinance.
Strict compliance would significantly reduce the buildable area of the lot, rendering
development economically infeasible and effectively precluding any reasonable use of the
property. The hardship is further attributable to the unique physical characteristics of the
parcel, rather than any action of the Applicant. The lot’s size and configuration, combined
with its prolonged vacancy, create conditions that are not generally applicable to other
